description: GAVII is a premier Registered Provider Organization (RPO) dedicated to simplifying cybersecurity and accelerating Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) compliance for the Defense Industrial Base (DIB). We equip your team with mandatory role-based CMMC compliance training, insider threat awareness, and simulated incident response exercises to ensure cybersecurity becomes an embedded part of your company culture. We also partner with CMMC authorized training providers to deliver CMMC certification training through our CMMCiQ platform. Post-Certification & Ongoing Support: We provide continuous monitoring guidance, change management support, and virtual advisory services to maintain your security posture as federal regulations and cyber threats evolve.

name: 8 Consulting, LLC
description: It's not Rocket Surgery... As small business owners in the government contracting business sector our inbox is filled every day with business requests just this side of predatory. Businesses trying to sell me on freely available government contracts, if I just pay them to get me on the GSA schedule. Offers of support in proposal development, often in emails poorly proofed. Offers to submit my business to the SBA as an 8a, which we could never qualify for. And one or two to teach my grandmother how to suck eggs. And now, the latest set of snake oil salesmen, the RPOs and MSPs that offer to get me through the Oh So Very Scary CMMC process. If only I give them a few hundred thousand dollars. And commit to an annual maintenance plan in the tens of thousands. So, here is the dirty truth… CMMC is not scary, it is not rocket surgery, and it should not be a significant economic or effort barrier to continuing to participate in DoD contract opportunities. There have been evolving policies, DFARS regulations, CMMC 1.0, CMMC 2.0, FAR proposed rules. This left us with a sour taste in our mouths, so we decided to see if we could take a little pain out of the world.

name: Almond Consulting Group, Inc.
description: Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) requirements are now written into Department of Defense (DoD) contracts. If your organization handles Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), a CMMC Level 2 assessment stands between you and contract eligibility, and assessment day is the wrong time to discover your System Security Plan (SSP) does not hold up. Almond Consulting Group, Inc. is a Cyber AB Registered Provider Organization (RPO) led by a Lead Certified CMMC Assessor (LCCA) , the credential required to lead the Certified Third-Party Assessment Organization (C3PAO) teams that conduct certification assessments. Most readiness providers advise from the implementer's side of the table. Almond Consulting prepares you from the assessor's side: every gap analysis, artifact, and interview prep reflects how your assessment will actually be scored. What that means on assessment day: Your gaps were found and closed months earlier, scored against the same assessment objectives a C3PAO uses Your SSP and Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) stand up to assessor scrutiny instead of just filling a template Your evidence is complete, organized, and mapped to NIST SP 800-171 requirements Your mock assessment was a true dress rehearsal, so nothing in the real one is a surprise Credentials behind the guidance: Almond Consulting has personnel holding the Registered Practitioner (RP), Certified CMMC Professional (CCP), Certified CMMC Assessor (CCA) and Lead Certified CMMC Assessor (LCCA) credentials, alongside Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP), Certified Information Security Manager (CISM), Certified in Risk and Information Systems Control (CRISC), Certified Data Privacy Solutions Engineer (CDPSE), Certified Ethical Hacker (CEH), Certified Network Defense Architect (CNDA), Certificate of Cloud Security Knowledge (CCSK), Navy Qualified Validator (NQV), Project Management Professional (PMP), Information Technology Infrastructure Library (ITIL), VMware Certified Professional in Data Center Virtualization (VCP-DCV), VMware Certified Professional in Network Virtualization (VCP-NV), Protected Distribution System (PDS), Six Sigma Black Belt, and Certified Scrum Master (CSM). That depth is backed by Risk Management Framework (RMF) packages and Authorizations to Operate (ATO) delivered on operational DoD systems, Security Control Assessor-Validator (SCA-V) experience, and a Secret facility clearance. Almond Consulting is a HUBZone-certified small business that builds readiness programs sized for small and mid-sized defense contractors. Know where you stand before your assessor does. Contact info@almondconsulting.com or visit www.almondconsulting.com

name: Awuah, Lawrence
description: As a Lead CCA, Lawrence is a passionate technology and cybersecurity SME with career-focused skills developed through practical and theoretical competencies in IT Compliance, Higher Ed, and Security Research. In other words, he brings a wealth of expertise gleaned from over a decade of work with a combination of teaching, research, and industry experiences. As a scholar-practitioner, Lawrence has vast experience spanning cybersecurity assessment, IT audit, networking, and electrical engineering domains of practice. Additionally, Lawrence is proud to be part of the CMMC Ecosystem and is dedicated to conducting CMMC assessments for the DoD DIB contractors, together with assisting with the select implementation of CMMC practices and compliance requirements through affiliation with C3PAO/RPO organizations. Consulting & Service Delivery: Lawrence is the founder and managing director of AbriteLogic Solutions, committed to providing vCISO and IT compliance services to small businesses with technical and executive-level guidance to help them secure their critical data and business investments. With relevant expertise, he regularly develops cybersecurity strategies, performs security assessments, conducts IT audits, and analyzes risk to help clients understand how risks impact their organizations and effective ways of safeguarding their assets. Teaching & Training Engagement: Lawrence has over 15 years of experience in Higher ED as an Adjunct Professor, teaching graduate and undergraduate degree courses while serving on various industry advisory boards and academic committees. He teaches and plays a key role in developing cybersecurity courses for undergraduate and graduate programs. Courses usually taught reflect key interdisciplinary areas such as security assessment, risk management, ethical hacking, penetration testing, digital forensics, and machine learning. Besides Higher Ed instructional obligations, Lawrence engages and trains employees and career changers in security awareness, designed to introduce learners to the basic concepts of cybersecurity and their usefulness in safeguarding user data, accounts, and assets. This training is used by IT and security professionals to prevent and mitigate user risk at home, the workplace, and remote locations. His ambition for sharing knowledge has earned him numerous accolades as a scholar-practitioner, advising, coaching, and inspiring learners in cybersecurity and threat intelligence domains of practice. Security Research: Lawrence's research interests and focus areas include, but are not limited to, machine intelligence (AI/ML), predictive analytics, security operations, incident response, risk management, and digital forensics. He routinely conducts applied research, develops test plans for assessing AI/ML model performance, and implements threat detection and intrusion prevention models to address potential cyber threats. His research papers have been published in several peer-reviewed journals. Academic Credentials: While he recently acquired CCA certification, Lawrence also holds other prestigious industry certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CISA, and ITIL. name: Baldwin, Jeff
description: Dr. Jeff Baldwin is a cybersecurity executive with an extensive background in both information security and education. As a senior information systems security engineer with over 19 years of cybersecurity experience, he has experience working in a variety of frameworks such as the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Risk Management Framework (RMF), DIACAP, NISPOM, DCID 6/3, and NISCAP. Dr. Baldwin has assessed over 150 systems as a Security Control Assessor, and as an Information Systems Security Engineer, he has helped over 100 government information systems achieve Authority to Operate (ATO) in cloud, hybrid, and traditional on-premises configurations as well as specialized embedded mission systems. Dr. Baldwin’s teaching experience includes over 15 years of teaching IT and IT Security courses at two nationally accredited state universities. Currently, he is an AWS Academy Accredited Educator. He is also a former Official (ISC)2 Instructor for the CISSP and ISSEP certifications. Besides his work experience with companies such as Tsymmetry, Leidos, L3Harris Technologies, GDIT, DigiFlight, and Battelle, he has served as volunteer President and Chairman for (ISC)2 Baltimore Chapter, and Vice President of Education for ISSA-NOVA. Dr. Baldwin earned a Doctor of Science in Cybersecurity and a Master of Science in Information Assurance from Capitol Technology University. He also earned a Bachelor of Technology in Information Technology: Network Administration with a minor in Application Software Development from SUNY College of Technology at Alfred. His relevant industry certifications include CISSP, ISSEP, ISSAP, CCSP, CISM, CISA, PMP, CSM, Cloud+, CySA+, and AWS Certified Solutions Architect Associate. As part of the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) ecosystem, Dr. Baldwin was one of the first 20 people to achieve both CMMC Provisional Instructor and Provisional Assessor status and had the privilege to be an instructor for the second ever offered CCP course.

name: Bautista, Wilson
description: Wilson Bautista is a retired military officer who is currently the founder and CEO of the consulting firm Jün Cyber, and the Executive Director of the Cyber Ohana Project, a Florida nonprofit corporation and registered 501(c)(3) organization. He provides expertise in the domains of InfoSec leadership, policy, architecture, compliance, and risk to his clients. He also has a Masters Degree in Information Systems Management from Boston University and a Masters of Business Administration from the University of South Florida. In the Marine Corps, Wilson led a Regimental level platoon of Marines in their deployment to Afghanistan. Deployed to Sangin, Afghanistan, he was responsible for supporting the maintenance of technology connectivity for over 1000 military and defense contracting personnel on the front lines. As a defense contractor for Headquarters Marine Corps, Wilson was responsible for preparing the Southeastern Marine Corps bases for their audit by the Defense Information Systems Agency. This included reviewing all physical security, Windows operating systems as well as, performing penetration testing of facilities and networks and vulnerability assessments. In preparation for their ISO 27001 certification and to become compliant to GDPR, Wilson built a global manufacturing company’s operational readiness practices including Vulnerability Management, Secure Configuration Management, Threat Management, and Web Application Security for the Global Information Security Organization. He worked across multiple service providers and created comprehensive plans of action and milestones after several security control assessments. Wilson was the virtual CISO for several businesses in the industries of lifesciences, academia, finance technology, defense industrial base, and data analytics where he developed and implemented a wide range of Cybersecurity and compliance related activities including building the Vulnerability Management program, SOC/SIEM practices, third-party security risk. Wilson holds active certifications in the following areas: HIPAA Security; Computer Systems Validation for the Lifesciences; CISSP; ISACA CISM, CISA, CRISC, CGEIT; ISO/IEC 27001 Senior Lead Implementer; Project Management Professional; TOGAF 9; CCSK, Computer System Validation-Life Science Industries.

Why Utilities & Critical Infrastructure Choose Me Domain-Appropriate Expertise Utilities combine legacy infrastructure, distributed field assets, and operational constraints. What Sets Me Apart (Differentiators) Utility-Focused Case Understanding Whether you're a municipal water utility, power distribution company, or energy provider with SCADA systems, I bring insights that generalist cybersecurity firms often lack. Clear Communication Across Stakeholders I translate between technical teams, operations, executive leadership, and regulators—ensuring all parties remain aligned. Flexible Engagement Models Whether you want project-based help, fractional CMMC support, or full lifecycle management, I adapt to fit. Ethical & Impartial Consulting I maintain strict boundaries from assessment providers, so you get candid advice, not biased recommendations. Scope & Gap Analysis Deep dive into architecture, control mappings, workflow gaps, and where CUI lives. name: Core Business Solutions, LLC.
description: Core Business Solutions helps small and mid-sized defense contractors achieve CMMC and NIST SP 800-171 compliance through a combination of consulting expertise, compliance tools, and a managed secure enclave solution called CORE Vault. CORE Vault is a purpose-built CMMC enclave designed specifically for organizations that must handle Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) but cannot afford the cost and complexity of rebuilding their entire IT infrastructure. The solution is deployed within the customer’s own AWS GovCloud account, allowing organizations to maintain full ownership and control of their environment and data while benefiting from a pre-configured, compliant technical architecture. The CORE Vault environment provides a secure workspace for handling CUI that includes virtual desktops, encrypted storage, secure email and file sharing, identity management, logging and monitoring, vulnerability scanning, and managed endpoint protection. The system is designed to support NIST SP 800-171 and CMMC Level 2 requirements while significantly reducing the scope and complexity of the compliance boundary. In addition to the secure enclave infrastructure, Core Business Solutions provides training, consulting, and compliance management tools through the CORE Compliance Platform. This web-based platform includes policy templates, compliance tracking, training modules, and automated tools that generate key documentation such as the System Security Plan (SSP), Plan of Action and Milestones (POAM), and SPRS score calculations. For over 25 years, Core Business Solutions has helped organizations implement and maintain management systems and regulatory compliance programs. The company is headquartered in Lewisburg, Pennsylvania and provides services nationwide through remote and onsite consulting resources. Core Business Solutions is certified to ISO 9001:2015 and ISO 27001:2022.

name: Epley, Wendy
description: Wendy Epley has worked in the Regulatory Trade Compliance field since 2008. She holds a Bachelor of Science degree in Global Business from Arizona State University. She also holds a Master of Science degree in Regulatory Trade Compliance. Part of her Master’s degree education included gaining an understanding of international export regimes including Canada, Australia, the European Union, and China. Her knowledge is always expanding. She maintains certification as an Export Compliance Professional (ECoP) and also holds several certifications and designations in export controls and the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) framework. She also achieved a Green Belt in Six Sigma DFSS. Her career expands working for Fortune 100 and Fortune 500 companies such as Honeywell Aerospace, Caterpillar, and Arthur Andersen LLP; however, since 2011 she has built a career in the higher education and research sector. In 2011, Wendy was the first Export Control Officer for the University of Miami where she built and managed the export control program for their three primary campuses. In 2015, she became the first Import and Export Compliance Officer for New York University where she oversaw the trade compliance program for the New York, Shanghai, and Abu Dhabi campuses. In late 2016, she returned to Arizona and supported the export control program at The University of Arizona (UArizona) until 2019. At that point in time, she was hired in a newly created position within the Information Security Office-Governance, Risk, and Compliance (ISO-GRC) team. As a Principal Analyst within the ISO-GRC, Wendy leads the Information Security in Contracting consultation services, manages the University Security Model of standards and frameworks, and the University's Cybersecurity Body of Risk Guardians (CyBoRG) community of practice. Wendy is an accomplished author of the Export Compliance and Foreign Corrupt Practices Act training programs with the Collaborative Institutional Training Initiative Program. She has also published articles in journals such as the National Council of University Research Administrators and WorldECR. She has presented at conferences and webinars on various issues surrounding export controls and cybersecurity compliance. She is actively involved with several organizations that support regulatory trade and cybersecurity compliance. Some of those include the Federated Cyber Risk Management Steering Committee sponsored by SibylSoft, the Regulated Research Community of Practice sponsored by the University of California San Diego, and several groups within the EDUCAUSE community. She also serves on the National Institute of Standards and Technology Generative AI Public Working Group. Her most recent appointment has been serving as the Ambassador of the American Chapter of the International Sanctions and Export Control Society. Wendy’s experience and background demonstrate she strongly supports sharing knowledge and helping others understand the nuanced world of governance, risk, and compliance.

name: Freitag, Aron
description: Aron Freitag Lead CMMC Assessor | CMMC, CCA Consultant | CISSP | Aron Freitag is a seasoned cybersecurity professional and Lead CMMC Assessor (CCA) with over 25 years of experience in U.S. military and Department of Defense (DoD) cybersecurity policy, standards, and risk management frameworks. His expertise spans NIST’s Risk Management Framework (800-53), Supply Chain Risk Management (800-161), and Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) protection in nonfederal systems (800-171). With a strong background in classified enclave security, Aron has successfully implemented, overseen, and accredited secure networks for critical DoD operations. He has extensive experience supporting multi-billion-dollar DoD and Army acquisition programs, ensuring robust security postures that meet federal compliance requirements. A U.S. Army veteran and former DoD civilian, Aron brings mission-driven leadership and deep technical expertise to his role, helping Defense Industrial Base (DIB) contractors navigate the complexities of CMMC certification. Holding a Bachelor of Science in Information Technology from Western Governors University and a CISSP certification, he is dedicated to strengthening national security through proactive risk management and cybersecurity best practices.

name: FRSecure
description: FRSecure is a full-service information security management company that protects sensitive, confidential business information from unauthorized access, disclosure, distribution, and destruction. Information security is not a one-size-fits-all as others would lead you to believe. FRSecure works hard to assess your most significant vulnerabilities (information security assessment), put a plan together for managing those risks (information security roadmap) and helps you execute that plan (information security program development). What makes FRSecure different? Mission Before Money: Our mission to fix the broken industry comes first. The priority has and always will be helping people. Whether it’s training, resources, or threat intelligence we will do our best to provide free tools to improve how we protect people’s data. Award-Winning Team: FRSecure takes pride in our team’s performance. As a company, we consistently win top workplace. We also win national awards based on customer satisfaction and our technical team dominates world hacking challenges at DEFCON. Universal Assessments: We didn’t like how anybody quantified risk so we built our own assessment. Our unique risk assessment methodology is based on NIST, maps to every major industry standard, and extends far beyond simple technical controls. Product Agnostic, On Purpose: We do not sell any third-party products, and security is all we do. Our advice will always be made with improving your security program in mind. We will never recommend hardware or software unless it’s what’s best for your organization.

description: One Partner Across the Full Compliance Lifecycle GovLynk's mission is to help small and mid-size businesses grow by winning and retaining U.S. Government contracts. Whether you're just getting started as a federal supplier or looking to expand an established government sales program, we meet you where you are and guide you forward. We specialize in two integrated service areas: Government Contracting and Compliance including CMMC — because in today's defense marketplace, you can't have one without the other. Government Contracting - From initial registration through ongoing opportunity development, GovLynk supports every stage of your federal contracting journey. Our team of seasoned experts helps you navigate SAM.gov registration, CAGE/UEI setup, SBA certifications, GSA Schedule and IDIQ contract vehicles, and proposal development. We leverage cutting-edge market intelligence to identify and pursue the opportunities best matched to your capabilities — building a sustainable government sales strategy designed for long-term growth. CMMC Compliance - As a CyberAB Registered Provider Organization (RPO) with Certified CMMC Professionals (CCP) and Registered Practitioners (RP) on staff, GovLynk provides trusted, accountable guidance through the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification process. For defense contractors handling Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), CMMC Level 2 certification is now a requirement — not an option. We guide you through scoping, gap assessment, SPRS scoring, SSP and POA&M development, and full C3PAO assessment readiness, so your compliance program strengthens your competitive position rather than slowing it down. At GovLynk, we believe that the path to government contracting success runs through both strategy and compliance. Our integrated approach means you have one trusted partner for the full journey — from your first federal registration to your next contract award.

name: Goyette, Joseph
description: Blue Mantle Technology (BMT) has a diverse clientele ranging from the federal government, including the Department of Defense (DoD) and various civilian agencies, to commercial organizations, which vary in both size and complexity. BMT specializes in delivering high quality information security solutions along with the Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) necessary to address even the most complicated information security needs. BMT's vast experience in the DoD sphere has provided us with a unique appreciation for the vital role a proper and thorough implementation of robust cybersecurity planning and practices play in the commercial world – especially in the world of government contracting with FAR, DFARs, NIST 800-171 and CMMC requirements. Our services are born out of securing some of the most targeted information systems in the world. BMT scales and tailors the demanding standards of the DoD and applies them to the needs of the commercial realm. Additionally, BMT is intimately familiar with the challenges and obligations present in the commercial cybersecurity domain, including, for example, the myriad compliance frameworks companies are bound by. These obligations can place heavy burdens on businesses who may lack the expertise to understand and implement the required controls. Let BMT and our team of experts relieve this weight. We have the knowledge and experience to secure your business, ensure compliance, and do so without “breaking the bank.” All of us, who have operated in the defense industrial base, understand the vital need to protect our countries intellectual property, our nation’s greatest assets, and contribute to our national defense. So, we understand the absolute need for CMMC. However, this does not minimize the difficulty it presents in its proper implementation and the burden it places on the business owner, especially the small business. BMT has the experience and expertise to lighten the load and help you and your team navigate the CMMC wilderness.

name: Gray, David
description: About Dave Gray Dave is one of the first CMMC Lead CCAs (CMMC Certified Assessor). Dave is one of the first CMMC Provisional Assessors to have complete the production CCP and CCA certifications. Dave Gray is the owner of CMMC Audit Pros LLC and DLG Consulting LLC. Dave is a CyberSecurity Leader skilled in securing information systems to achieve information Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability. Dave uses his LLC to consult, assess, and teach all things CMMC. Dave provides pre-assessment consulting directly and CMMC-certified assessment in partnership with C3PAOs. Dave achieved CMMC Provisional Assessor (PA) status in the first CMMC PA course in September 2020 followed by CMMC Provisional Instructor (PI) status in June 2021. Certified CMMC Assessor, CMMC Instructor, CCP, CCA, CISSP, CGRC (CAP), PMP, Security+ ce, and CEH Information Technology Leader skilled in securing information systems to achieve information confidentiality, integrity, and availability. As a thought leader in the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) ecosystem, Dave consults, assesses, and teaches CMMC Federal Contract Information (FCI) and Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) cybersecurity to meet Department of Defense (DoD) compliance requirements for DFARS 252.204-7012. Dave regularly consults for DoD vendors regarding the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Department of Defense (DoD) Assessment Methodology. Dave promotes Cybersecurity as a key enabler for Defense Industrial Base (DIB) success, aligning effort levels with outcomes through consulting, assessing, and teaching cybersecurity courses. Dave's certifications include: CMMC Lead Certified Assessor (CCA) CMMC Certified Assessor (CCA) CMMC Certified Professional (CCP) CMMC Provisional Instructor (PI) CISSP – Certified Information Systems Security Professional CGRC – CGRC – Governance, Risk and Compliance Certification (formerly CAP – Certified Authorization Professional) ITIL – Information Technology Infrastructure Library PMP – Project Management Professional CEH – Certified Ethical Hacker Security+ ce Dave regularly teaches CyberAB CAICO approved CCP and CCA courses in-person and online for multiple Licensed Training Providers (LTP) each month, providing a choice of training organizations for students to work through. Dave is available for corporate training using CMMC Approved Training Material (CATM) for persons seeking certification or custom material for persons seeking to expand their CMMC knowledge. name: Houser, Elizabeth
description: SimIS, Inc. provides cybersecurity, CMMC readiness, and secure IT modernization services for organizations supporting federal, defense, and regulated missions. Founded in 2007, SimIS is a Veteran Owned Small Business that helps clients model the future, secure the enterprise, and strengthen mission outcomes through disciplined processes, integrated architecture, and practical technology solutions. SimIS brings together information security consulting, engineering, government services experience, and operational cybersecurity expertise to help Defense Industrial Base organizations move from uncertainty to a defensible CMMC and NIST SP 800-171 readiness position. Our approach is practical, evidence-driven, and built around the realities of small and mid-sized organizations that must protect Federal Contract Information, Controlled Unclassified Information, mission data, and contract eligibility without losing sight of day-to-day business operations. We do not treat CMMC as a documentation exercise or a one-time compliance project. We help organizations understand their scope, identify what must be protected, close security gaps, build credible documentation, develop assessment-ready evidence, and establish the governance routines needed to sustain cybersecurity improvements over time. Core Service Offerings CMMC and NIST SP 800-171 Readiness SimIS supports organizations preparing for CMMC and NIST SP 800-171 requirements through scoping, applicability analysis, gap assessments, remediation planning, evidence development, and readiness preparation. We help clients understand what applies, where sensitive information resides, which controls need attention, and what must be demonstrated before an assessment. Secure Cloud and Microsoft 365 Services We design, secure, and support Microsoft 365 and cloud environments that improve collaboration while protecting sensitive business and contract data. Our support includes identity, device management, collaboration, access control, and data handling models aligned to regulated and defense-related operations. SharePoint and Collaboration Governance SimIS helps organizations structure SharePoint, Teams, and document workflows so information is stored, shared, and governed the right way. We focus on usability, ownership, permissions, document control, secure information handling, and evidence organization so collaboration environments support both operations and compliance. Cyber Risk Assessment and Remediation We identify the security gaps that matter most and help organizations fix them in a practical, business-aligned way. Our services include vulnerability assessment support, control gap analysis, remediation planning, technical hardening, and prioritization based on risk, mission impact, and assessment readiness. Governance, Evidence, and Sustainment CMMC readiness depends on more than tools and policies. SimIS helps organizations build ownership, recurring review routines, evidence practices, and internal accountability so security improvements remain in place over time. We help clients move from “we think we do this” to “we can prove how this works.” IT Modernization and Operational Hardening SimIS supports modernization of legacy and organically grown IT environments through improved access control, endpoint management, secure configuration, backup, logging, and operational IT governance. We help organizations strengthen the IT foundation that CMMC and long-term cyber resilience depend on.

description: KAMIND IT is a CMMC Level 2 Certified and Cyber AB Registered Provider Organization (RPO), delivering trusted cybersecurity and compliance solutions for defense contractors and government-focused businesses. name: Keeler, James
description: James has been conducting NIST 800-171 gap assessments for businesses in the Defense Industrial Base (DIB) since 2019, and has been actively following the evolution from self-attested implementation of the NIST 800-171 controls under the DFARS 252.204-7012 clause to the launch of the CMMC program from CMMC v1.0 to the current state today. As the NIST 800-171 & CMMC ecosystem have evolved, he has assisted many businesses in the DIB with gap assessments, technical implementation guidance, audit preparedness, policy writing, personnel training, and business process alignment to allow the complex security requirements of NIST 800-171 to be implemented without undue burden to their operational efficiency in a cost-sensitive fashion. With a background in government and academia IT followed by over 10 years of incident response work in the private sector, James is well positioned to understand the cybersecurity and business requirements related to government contracting cybersecurity and the threat landscape faced by DIB members. Additionally, his understanding of manufacturing environment challenges from legacy equipment, operational technology (OT) specific challenges, to supply chain risk management provide significant value in helping organizations with these complex environments manage the resulting unique risk and compliance concerns. In addition to leading NIST 800-171 assessments, System Security Plan (SSP) and Plan of Action and Milestone (PoAM) development, DFARS cybersecurity requirement fulfillment, supplier management, and SPRS registration & score entry; James provides members of the DIB with consulting expertise encompassing cybersecurity, information technology, business process, and human behavior that reduces the friction experienced when making the transformation to the security-first mode of operations that CMMC compliance requires.

description: Why Choose KLC Consulting We understand the natural apprehension people feel going into their high-stakes CMMC assessment. You worry you'll get the invasive "gotcha!" type of auditor. Our assessment philosophy is to be the objective C3PAO that validates your demonstrated security practices without digging deeper in search of flaws, ensuring an assessment delivered with a clear understanding and the human touch. We're now scheduling CMMC Assessments The CMMC ecosystem faces an acute supply-demand imbalance: For every 1,000 organizations seeking certification, there's only about 1 authorized C3PAO to assess them! Given this scarcity, scheduling your CMMC Certification Assessment as soon as possible is of the utmost importance. Please use our Calendar link to schedule a Zoom call at your convenience. You can also reach us at cmmc@klcconsulting.net or call 617-314-9721 x158. CMMC ASSESSMENT SERVICES CMMC Level 2 Mock (Readiness) Assessment Are you in doubt about your CMMC Level 2 Assessment? Our CMMC Mock Assessment illuminates the path to compliance by providing a realistic simulation of an official CMMC Level 2 Certification Assessment like the full-contact scrimmage teams play to prepare for an in-season game. This lower-priced practice-run assessment brings the full intensity and scrutiny of an Official Level 2 assessment, identifying and explaining deficiencies from an independent C3PAO perspective. It's designed to empower your team's self-remediation efforts and build confidence for success in your official Level 2 assessment. Ask about your discount for a Mock-Official CMMC Level 2 Assessment Bundle and Low-Cost Limited Mock Assessment options to prepare for your POA&M Closeout Assessment. CMMC Level 2 Assessment A CMMC Assessment is a formal compliance evaluation by an independent C3PAO that verifies an organization's implementation of CMMC practices. It's the Department of Defense's way of ensuring Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) is protected. You've put in the hard work to prepare, and KLC Consulting respects that commitment. Our interactive collaborative approach helps you clearly understand each part of the process, including how we determine your compliance score and status. We'll also thoroughly explain provisions designed to benefit you, such as the 10-day window for correcting minor, non-systemic deficiencies after your assessment. POA&M Closeout Assessment Attaining Conditional Status (an assessment score between 88 and 109) in your CMMC Level 2 Certification Assessment means you've implemented many, but not all, required practices. CMMC allows up to 180 days to remediate and validate identified deficiencies through a POA&M Closeout Assessment. KLC Consulting provides fast, inexpensive closeout assessments scaled directly to the number of non-compliant practices that need reassessment. INDUSTRY-SPECIFIC CMMC ASSESSMENTS Defense Prime Contractors & System Integrators Assessing organizations with complex, multi-divisional structures and expansive Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) scopes across diverse hybrid infrastructures demands highly specialized C3PAO expertise. KLC Consulting possesses extensive direct experience with these intricate environments, including those heavily reliant on Secure Software Development Life Cycles (SSDLCs). Our depth of knowledge far exceeds foundational C3PAO requirements and the capabilities of most C3PAOs in the marketplace today, ensuring a precise assessment for even the most advanced operational contexts. IT Managed Service Providers (MSPs) We appreciate that IT Managed Service Providers play a critical role in the defense supply chain, managing complex environments and CUI for multiple clients. KLC Consulting possesses direct experience assessing MSP operations, recognizing the nuances of shared infrastructure, multi-tenant architectures, and CUI flow-down within your unique service delivery model. Defense Software Developers Assessing organizations that develop software for Department of Defense (DoD) applications requires rare, specialized knowledge. KLC Consulting possesses deep expertise in evaluating Secure Software Development Life Cycles (SSDLCs) and DevSecOps environments. We understand precisely how Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) should be handled and protected within codebases, design specifications, and continuous integration/delivery pipelines. We provide the thorough technical capability to accurately assess your unique development processes and intellectual property. Manufacturers Manufacturers operate with distinct technological landscapes, frequently utilizing on-premises IT systems, hybrid environments, and legacy components . Assessing CMMC compliance within these operational technologies (OT) and interconnected physical environments presents unique challenges. KLC Consulting possesses hands-on experience assessing manufacturing IT infrastructures giving us the insight needed to assess your specific operational complexities. Architects, Engineers, and Professional Services Firms Architects, engineers, and other professional services firms often handle Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) within cloud-based environments. KLC Consulting excels at assessing these cloud-centric operations. A significant benefit for organizations with no physical CUI stored, processed, or transmitted at their facilities is the ability to conduct assessments entirely remotely reducing assessment time and price. name: Kratos Technology & Training Solutions
description: As a CMMC Third Party Assessment Organization (C3PAO), Kratos teams are ready to conduct the CMMC assessments that are a prerequisite to CMMC 2.0 certification. CMMC 2.0 streamlines the process, reduces costs, and improves flexibility. Kratos’ assessment process consists of up to four phases and, depending on complexity, most assessments will be completed in four to six weeks. Much of the progress Organizations Seeking Certification (OSC) and Defense Industrial Base (DIB) members have taken will still apply and ease CMMC certification. CMMC 2.0 still addresses security concerns related to Federal Contract Information (FCI) and Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and divides certification levels based on what type of information an organization handles. CMMC 2.0 does not alter the Level 1 controls, but only requires a self-attestation for Level 1 certification. Certified C3PAOs are still able to assess or offer advisory services. Kratos has years of robust compliance and certification experience with government and commercial standards requirements. Kratos is viewed as a trusted compliance and governance partner by the Department of Defense (DoD), Federal Civilian Agencies, Intelligence Community (IC), and commercial organizations. Kratos cybersecurity services include Compliance, Governance, Risk Management & Strategy and Cyber: Operations, Defense, & Engineering services. description: Dr. Minjae Lee is the President and CEO of TQMS Co., Ltd., and a recognized authority on cybersecurity maturity and compliance in the Republic of Korea. description: Professional Overview – Eric Lunsford, CCA, CCP, RPA, RP Mr. Eric Lunsford is a CMMC Registered Practitioner (RP), CMMC Registered Practitioner Advanced (RPA), Certified CMMC Professional (CCP), and CMMC Certified Assessor (CCA) . With this combination of credentials, Mr. Lunsford is uniquely positioned to deliver both formal assessments and strategic consulting services within the Department of Defense (DoD) Defense Industrial Base (DIB) Supply Chain . His professional mission is to help contractors and subcontractors align their cybersecurity programs with federal regulatory and compliance requirements , ensuring the protection of Federal Contract Information (FCI) and Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) across the supply chain. Expertise and Compliance Knowledge Mr. Lunsford’s expertise extends across multiple regulatory and cybersecurity frameworks, including but not limited to: Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC 2.0) – Compliance readiness, gap analysis, policy and control implementation, and formal CCA assessments. NIST SP 800-171 – Protecting CUI in nonfederal systems through technical and procedural safeguards. NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 – Security and privacy controls for information systems supporting federal operations. NIST Risk Management Framework (RMF) – Full lifecycle support for categorization, control selection, assessment, authorization, and continuous monitoring. DFARS 252.204-7012/7019/7020/7021 – DoD contracting cybersecurity clauses governing reporting, safeguarding, and assessments. FedRAMP & ISO/IEC 27001 – Governance alignment for organizations leveraging cloud-based or international security frameworks. Professional Roles and Experience Mr. Lunsford has served in several critical roles within the cybersecurity and compliance field, including: Virtual Chief Information Security Officer (vCISO): Advising executive leadership on compliance strategy, cyber risk management, and long-term governance planning. Senior Security Engineer: Designing, implementing, and maintaining secure infrastructures for DoD contractors. Secure Infrastructure Specialist: Building resilient architectures with encryption, access control, and monitoring aligned to DoD requirements. Project Manager: Leading cross-functional teams in the deployment of cybersecurity solutions, compliance documentation, and audit readiness projects. Security Operations Center (SOC) Analyst: Conducting incident detection, response, and continuous monitoring in mission-critical environments. Track Record of Success Mr. Lunsford has delivered regulatory and compliance assistance to over 100+ organizations within the DoD Defense Industrial Base (DIB) . His engagements span from small businesses seeking CMMC Level 1 compliance to mid- and large-scale contractors preparing for CMMC Level 2 and beyond. Key areas of assistance include: Supplier Performance Risk Score (SPRS): Improving and validating self-assessments to strengthen contractor competitiveness in the DoD marketplace. Federal Contract Information (FCI): Establishing safeguards to meet FAR 52.204-21 minimum standards. Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI): Ensuring proper handling, storage, and transmission protections per NIST 800-171 requirements. Network Security: Deploying modern architectures with Zero Trust, segmentation, and monitoring. Device Configurations: Hardening endpoints, servers, and mobile devices in alignment with CIS benchmarks and DoD STIGs. Commitment to the Defense Industrial Base Through his combined roles as an Assessor, Consultant, and Cybersecurity Strategist , Mr. Lunsford provides end-to-end support to organizations navigating the complex regulatory landscape of DoD contracting. His approach blends technical expertise, governance strategy, and real-world experience , ensuring that companies not only meet compliance requirements but also strengthen their overall security posture. For more information or to schedule an assessment/consulting session, contact Mr. Lunsford directly at 704-252-9868. Eric Lunsford – Protecting DoD Supply Chains, One Contractor at a Time.

Our business model entails our customers offering our SurveyFirst™ questionnaire tool to members of a cohort, trade association or similarly situated group members to establish an average or composite score of the group as a whole. name: Manuel, Anthony
description: From System Stability to CMMC Compliance: Ensuring Your DoD Business is Secure, Resilient, and Ready. Are you a small to mid-tier defense contractor facing the CMMC initiative? The CMMC can be overwhelming, with its technical controls seemingly unrelated to your operations. My approach to CMMC is different. With over two decades of hands-on IT system analysis and business process governance, I can connect the dots between seemingly disparate controls. I don’t just evaluate controls, I ensure they’re seamlessly integrated into your IT systems, which operate your business. How my experience can benefit you: Operational Security Mindset: In my previous position, I was responsible for ensuring 100% uptime SLAs, as well as leading Disaster Recovery testing. This experience in ensuring business continuity is instrumental in implementing effective CMMC controls in Incident Response and System Integrity. From Gap Analysis to Execution: I just completed a full CMMC Level 2 readiness assessment for a new client, where I was able to map 110 NIST 800-171 practices against their business and develop a prioritized roadmap for execution. I also wrote the client’s System Security Plan (SSP), where I took the results of the assessment and created a living document for compliance. Speaking Both Languages: As a former Senior Business Analyst, I am skilled at communicating technical needs in a way that all stakeholders can understand. I can communicate the “why” of a particular control to the business leadership and the “how” of implementation to your IT staff. Technical Credibility: As a current degree program focused on cybersecurity, I am working with tools like Metasploit and Wireshark. I am also a Registered Practitioner (RP), the official designation from the CMMC. I understand the threats you are trying to protect against. I help companies like yours, where the IT staff is often asked to wear many hats, develop a compliant, secure, and efficient business environment that meets the needs of the DoD. Let’s connect and discuss your particular situation and the first steps towards a stress-free certification process. CMMC Readiness Discovery Questionnaire

description: Perezdiaz, LLC CMMC Third-Party Assessment Organization (C3PAO) Perezdiaz, LLC is an independent cybersecurity assessment organization specializing in third-party evaluation of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) protection programs across the Defense Industrial Base (DIB). The firm is structured to deliver objective, evidence-based CMMC assessments aligned with the CMMC Assessment Process (CAP), 32 CFR Part 170, and Cyber AB requirements. The organization is led by experienced assessment professionals with deep backgrounds in government, defense, and regulated commercial environments. Perezdiaz, LLC operates with a strict commitment to assessor independence, assessment integrity, and conflict-of-interest discipline. CMMC Assessment Focus Perezdiaz, LLC performs independent CMMC Level 2 assessments for Organizations Seeking Assessment (OSAs), including environments with: Hybrid and cloud-based enclaves On-premises manufacturing and operational technology (OT) systems Controlled facilities and mixed-use environments Distributed workforces and alternate worksites Assessment activities emphasize traceability, evidence sufficiency, and control intent rather than documentation-only compliance. Assessment Methodology & Rigor The firm applies a disciplined, regulator-first assessment methodology that includes: Full alignment to NIST SP 800-171 assessment objectives Evidence validation across technical, administrative, and physical controls Risk-based evaluation consistent with DoD and Cyber AB guidance Clear determination of POA&M eligibility , including identification of non-POA&M-eligible requirements CAP-aligned reporting and defensible certification recommendations Assessments are conducted to withstand DoD review, quality audits, and downstream contractual scrutiny. Independence & Conflict-of-Interest Controls Perezdiaz, LLC maintains strict separation between third-party assessment activities and any advisory or readiness services performed by affiliated entities. The organization enforces: Compliance with Cyber AB Code of Professional Conduct Formal conflict-of-interest screening prior to assessment engagement Assessor role separation to preserve objectivity No remediation, implementation, or consulting influence during assessments This structure protects the integrity of the certification process and ensures impartial outcomes for OSAs. Assessment Team Qualifications (In-House) Perezdiaz, LLC maintains qualified assessment personnel with the following credentials held in-house or equivalent , as applicable to role and engagement scope: Lead Certified CMMC Assessor (CCA) Certified CMMC Assessor (CCA) Certified CMMC Professional (CCP) Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA) Certified in Risk and Information Systems Control (CRISC) Certificate of Cloud Security Knowledge (CCSK) ITIL Foundation Lean Six Sigma (Green Belt or equivalent) Assessment team members possess prior experience supporting high-consequence cybersecurity assessments, including DIBCAC High Assessments and enterprise-scale CUI programs. Governance, Quality, and Oversight Perezdiaz, LLC incorporates internal governance and quality assurance practices to support consistent assessment outcomes, including: Assessment peer review and quality checks Assessor calibration and ongoing training Controlled evidence handling and documentation standards Continuous alignment with evolving DoD and Cyber AB guidance These practices ensure assessments remain repeatable, defensible, and compliant with current regulatory expectations. Defense & Government Experience The organization’s leadership and assessment staff bring prior experience supporting U.S. Department of Defense and federal mission environments, including national-level mission assurance, secure communications, continuity operations, and inter-agency coordination. This background informs a practical understanding of operational risk, mission impact, and regulatory accountability. Organizational Assessment Philosophy Perezdiaz, LLC approaches CMMC assessments with a singular objective: to provide the DoD with accurate, independent, and defensible certification decisions . Assessments are conducted fairly, consistently, and without bias, enabling contracting authorities to rely on certification outcomes with confidence.

name: PRIVAXI, LLC
description: PRIVAXI Technologies is a CMMC Registered Practitioner Organization (RPO) built for defense contractors who want more than a gap report. We are practitioners first — engineers, assessors-by-training, and embedded vCISOs who do the actual work of CMMC readiness: scoping your CUI environment, implementing NIST SP 800-171 controls, writing your policies and procedures, authoring your SSP and POA&M, calculating and submitting your SPRS score, penetration testing your environment, packaging assessment evidence, and standing beside you through your C3PAO assessment. What sets PRIVAXI apart: Hands-On Technical Delivery — Not Advisory-Only. Many RPOs deliver findings and walk away. PRIVAXI engineers remediation alongside your team. We configure controls, harden environments, design CUI enclaves, and build the documentation a C3PAO will actually accept. When your assessor asks for evidence, it's already organized, mapped, and defensible. CYRIK — Our Purpose-Built CMMC Operations Platform. CYRIK centralizes control tracking, evidence management, remediation workflow, third-party risk, and continuous monitoring in one place, keeping you assessment-ready at all times — not scrambling in the 90 days before your assessment. CYRIK operates as an External Service Provider supporting your environment; your data stays within your boundaries. CAMP360 — Compliance-as-a-Service, Year-Round. Certification is a moment; compliance is a lifecycle. Our Continuous Assurance Management Program (CAMP360) maintains your posture after certification with continuous control monitoring, evidence refresh, change management, and annual affirmation support — so Year 2 and Year 3 are as strong as Day 1. Engineer Once, Report Many. Most defense contractors don't live in a single framework. Our proprietary cluster methodology maps your control environment once across CMMC/NIST 800-171, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, HITRUST, and PCI DSS — so a single engineering effort satisfies multiple contractual and regulatory obligations without duplicate cost. Complete Policy & Procedure Authorship. Documentation is where most assessments fail. PRIVAXI writes your full CMMC documentation library from the ground up — security policies, operational procedures, plans, and supporting artifacts — mapped control-by-control to NIST SP 800-171 and written to reflect how your organization actually operates, not boilerplate templates a C3PAO will see through. Every document is assessment-ready and maintained as your environment changes. Penetration Testing & Technical Validation. We don't just claim your controls work — we prove it. PRIVAXI delivers penetration testing and vulnerability assessments against your CUI environment, validating that implemented controls hold up under real adversarial pressure and producing the technical evidence that strengthens your assessment package and your actual security posture. SHIELDSOC — 24/7 Security Operations. CMMC requires operational security, not just paperwork. SHIELDSOC delivers 24/7 SOC/SIEM monitoring, detection, and response that directly satisfies audit, monitoring, and incident response control families — with the logs and evidence to prove it. 25+ Years of Practitioner Expertise. Our leadership has spent more than two decades in cybersecurity, risk, and regulatory compliance across defense, healthcare, and financial sectors. We've watched the threat landscape and the regulatory landscape evolve in parallel — and we build programs that survive both. Clear, Conflict-Free Role. As an RPO, PRIVAXI provides readiness, implementation, documentation, and advisory services. We are not a C3PAO and do not perform certification assessments — which means zero conflict of interest and total alignment with one outcome: you passing your assessment the first time. Whether you're a Level 1 contractor self-assessing or a Level 2 organization preparing for a C3PAO assessment, PRIVAXI operates as an extension of your team — technical, accountable, and invested in your result.

Regola Cyber is based in the National Capital Region, local to Baltimore, Northern Virginia (NOVA), and Washington D.C. We support Organizations Seeking Certification (OSCs) in Maryland, D.C., Virginia, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and nationwide. We work both on-site and virtually, always following C3PAO ethical and independence standards.

name: Schaaff, Kevin
description: Kevin Schaaff is a cybersecurity professional with an extensive background in both information security, training, and education. As a Principal Systems Engineer with over 24 years of cybersecurity experience supporting the Intelligence Community, he has experience working with a variety of frameworks including the CERT® Resilience Management Model (CERT-RMM), National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Risk Management Framework (RMF), NISCAP, DCID 6/3, NISPOM, ISO 9001, ISO 27001, CMMI, and DIACAP. Kevin has assessed over 100 systems as a Certified High Maturity Lead Appraiser, and dozens of organizations as an ISO Lead Auditor. As a Principal Systems Engineer, he has helped designed and build numerous information systems for DoD and the Intelligence Community in cloud, hybrid, and traditional on-premises configurations including command and control and combat systems. Kevin’s teaching experience includes over 30 years of developing curriculum and teaching courses in Agile, Project Management, CMMI, and IT Security for several DoD prime contractors, DoD and Civil Agencies and the Intelligence Community. Currently, he is also a Certified CMMI Instructor and supports the development of ISACA training courses. He has also assisted with test development for the CCA and CCP certifications. His work experience includes 24 years in the US Navy, the Software Engineering Institute, Booz Allen Hamilton, Northrop Grumman, CMMI Institute, and ISACA. Kevin earned a Master of Science in Engineering Acoustics and a Master of Science in Applied Science from the Naval Postgraduate School. He also earned a Bachelor of Science from the United States Naval Academy. His relevant industry certifications include CISSP, PMP, CCA, CHMLA, and CCP. As part of the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) ecosystem, Kevin was one of the first group of people to achieve both CMMC Provisional Instructor and Provisional Assessor status. Kevin was the ISACA representative on the panel that provided initial recommendations to the Government team who created the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC). He was also a member of the initial industrial group that authored the first version of the CMMC Assessment Process. Kevin and his wife reside in Jacksonville, FL, and have two sons that are security engineers; one supporting the Intelligence Community and one supporting a global technology company. Kevin has worked in or traveled to over 68 countries.

name: Shellproof
description: Choosing a compliance partner is a major investment. Defense contractors choose Shellproof because we don't just hand you a checklist we deliver a clear, predictable path to certification without disrupting your business. 1. We Bridge the Gap to Advanced Frameworks We don't look at CMMC in a vacuum. Our readiness assessments are built natively around NIST SP 800-171, creating a seamless, logical bridge to advanced compliance frameworks like CMMC Level 2 and FedRAMP . Furthermore, we understand how these controls interlink with ISO 27001 and SOC 2 . We map your security controls intelligently so you can meet multiple compliance goals without duplicating work or paying twice. 2. We Demystify and Simplify NIST Standards NIST and CMMC documentation can be dense and overwhelming. We translate complex regulatory requirements into plain, actionable language. Whether you are dealing with traditional encryption protocols or implementing modern, AI-based security controls, we break down exactly what is required so your IT team can execute with confidence. 3. Proven, Audit-Aligned Methodologies We don't guess what auditors want; we use the exact same defined methodologies, assessment guides, and scoping rules that official C3PAO auditors use. By conducting rigorous mock assessments using true-to-life audit criteria, we ensure your team experiences zero surprises and zero costly delays during your formal evaluation. 4. Flexible Offerings to Fit Your Business Every defense contractor has a unique footprint, budget, and timeline. We don't force you into a rigid, one-size-fits-all consulting package. Shellproof provides highly flexible service tiers—ranging from quick, budget-conscious gap assessments to comprehensive, end-to-end readiness advisory—tailored entirely to your operational realities. The Bottom Line: Shellproof transforms compliance from a stressful business bottleneck into a competitive differentiator. We ensure your security posture is robust, your team is confident, and your organization is fully equipped to win and protect critical DoD contracts.

name: Slocum, Brigham
description: Blue Mantle Technology (BMT) has a diverse clientele ranging from the federal government, including the Department of Defense (DoD) and various civilian agencies, to commercial organizations, which vary in both size and complexity. BMT specializes in delivering high quality information security solutions along with the Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) necessary to address even the most complicated information security needs. BMT's vast experience in the DoD sphere has provided us with a unique appreciation for the vital role a proper and thorough implementation of robust cybersecurity planning and practices play in the commercial world – especially in the world of government contracting with FAR, DFARs, NIST 800-171 and CMMC requirements. Our services are born out of securing some of the most targeted information systems in the world. BMT scales and tailors the demanding standards of the DoD and applies them to the needs of the commercial realm. Additionally, BMT is intimately familiar with the challenges and obligations present in the commercial cybersecurity domain, including, for example, the myriad compliance frameworks companies are bound by. These obligations can place heavy burdens on businesses who may lack the expertise to understand and implement the required controls. Let BMT and our team of experts relieve this weight. We have the knowledge and experience to secure your business, ensure compliance, and do so without “breaking the bank.” All of us, who have operated in the defense industrial base, understand the vital need to protect our countries intellectual property, our nation’s greatest assets, and contribute to our national defense. So, we understand the absolute need for CMMC. However, this does not minimize the difficulty it presents in its proper implementation and the burden it places on the business owner, especially the small business. BMT has the experience and expertise to lighten the load and help you and your team navigate the CMMC wilderness.

description: SysAudits, LLC is a small minority owned company located in Virginia that specializes in offering exceptional service involving information technology security audits. Contact info: info@sysaudits.com. SysAudits staff and ownership is composed of skilled auditors with certifications as Certified Public Accountants (CPA), Certified Information Systems Auditor’s (CISA), Certified in Risk and Information Systems Control (CRISC), and Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP). We believe our skill mix and mind set of understanding technology and business risks, costs, and internal controls is found to be beneficial for both the Audit department and the Technology operations side of an organization. We specialize in performing and assessing system audits for government (Federal, State, Local, Non-Profits, and Education) as well as the commercial sector. Serves Offered: SysAudits system security services include regulatory gap/pre-assessments, network assessments, general system administration controls, security solution support, audit liaison support, and many other IT cyber assessments. More specifically, our services are directed towards performing regulatory assessments, readiness assessments involving NIST 171, 800-53, FISMA, HiTrust, ITAR, and many others. FISMA/ITAR/ CMMC/ HIPAA /HiTrust Assessments and Audits The Federal Information Security Management Act ( FISMA ) is a federal law under the E-Gov Act that was enacted to increase the security posture of government agency federal systems, bureaus, departments and their supporting entities. For Federal agencies that are required to comply with FISMA, the requirement extends to compliance with their 3rd party providers which may include outsourced data centers, application providers, and cloud service providers. International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) control the export and import of defense-related articles and services on the United States Munitions List (USML). Overseen by the U.S. State Department, U.S. Commerce Department, and Department of Defense, ITAR data must be protected and restricted under NIST 171 guidance. DOD CMMC and NIST 171 security control assessment for Levels 1-3. Perform readiness assessments for compliance with mandated policies, procedures, design, and implementation of the 120+ security controls. Assist organizations in designing and implementing the security controls. Assist organizations through knowledge transfer to support enhanced policies, procedures, and operations to meet CMMC controls. The HiTrust and Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act ( HIPAA ). HIPAA was enacted by Congress in 1996 with the Security Rule in place as a methodology to safeguard electronic Protected Health Information. HIPAA applies to healthcare providers, plans, and clearinghouses, (known as covered entities), and any organization contracted by covered entities to perform work including ePHI (business associates). The HIPAA Security Rule is based on three types of security safeguards (physical, technical, and administrative. HiTrust is an independent certification for HIPAA and SysAudits has assisted organizations in HiTrust readiness assessment, gap assessment, and audit liaison support. SysAudits offers a variety of services to assist in meeting regulatory compliance from an operational Office of CIO and an Inspector General (IG) audit perspective. OCIO pre-assessments can assist IT leadership in identifying weaknesses in meeting regulatory and assist in developing plans of actions and milestones prior to an Audit assessment. The value in an internal self-assessment is identifying weaknesses prior to an external audit. Audit assessments are clearly performed as an independent audit to determine an organization compliance in meeting regulatory requirements. SysAudits staff have extensive experience on both the Audit and CIO perspective. This perspective brings value in performing pre-assessments and audits which makes SysAudits stand out amongst other consulting firms. SysAudits methodology consists of assessing, testing and reviewing information systems through in-depth assessment of NIST defined management, operational, and technical testing of controls. The following represents services provided by SysAudits: NIST 171, ITAR and CMMC compliance NIST 800-53 compliance FIPS 199 categorization, FIPS 200 and agency control selection. Security controls assessment. Authorization recommendation of system and continuous monitoring. Security Assessment Plan (SAP), Rules of Engagement (ROE), and Security Assessment Report (SAR) development. Vulnerability Management and Continuous Monitoring Penetration testing. Internal Vulnerability testing. Wireless and mobile security assessments. Application, database, and infrastructure vulnerability scanning and results interpretation. Architecture and system boundary assessments. Secure configuration management administration and operations. Network design and third-party service provider evaluations. Contingency system planning and additional guidance based on your agency’s requirements. Compliance program pre-assessments. FISMA documentation development, including System Security Plan (SSP), Contingency Plan (CP), Incident Response Plan (IRP), Configuration Management Plan (CMP), Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA), and FIPS 199 Security Categorization, Policies, Procedures, etc. IT Audits SysAudits has extensive experience in performing all types of IT audits that include audits of: Vulnerability management programs. System development life cycle for new applications and enhancements. IT Contracting and procurement. IT Contract re-design, consolidation, and enterprise re-architect of enterprise IT contracts. IT contract investigation and litigation support: cost mischarging; contract close outs under terminations for convenience and performance. IT policy and procedures. Headquartered in the Tampa Bay / St. Petersburg, Florida region, Jun Cyber supports small and mid-sized defense contractors, subcontractors, and regulated manufacturers that handle Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and must meet NIST SP 800-171 and CMMC requirements . What We Do Jun Cyber focuses on execution-driven compliance , not advisory-only consulting. Our services are designed to move organizations from uncertainty to audit-ready with defensible evidence. Core services include: CMMC Level 1 & Level 2 Readiness NIST SP 800-171 Gap Assessments System Security Plan (SSP) & POA&M Development Control Implementation Oversight Evidence Collection & Validation Pre-Assessment & Audit Preparation Ongoing Compliance & Continuous Monitoring Managed Compliance as a Service (MCaaS) Differentiation Jun Cyber is led by a Certified CMMC Assessor (CCA) with real-world experience operating compliance programs inside complex, regulated environments—not just advising from the outside. Key differentiators: Operational focus : We help clients run compliance programs, not just document them. Technology-aligned controls : SSPs and POA&Ms are mapped to actual tools and configurations in use. White-label delivery model : Trusted execution partner for MSPs and consulting firms delivering CMMC services to their clients. Defense-first mindset : Familiarity with DFARS, CUI data flows, enclave scoping, and DoD expectations. Who We Serve Defense contractors and subcontractors Aerospace, manufacturing, and engineering firms MSPs and compliance consultancies needing delivery capacity Organizations pursuing or maintaining CMMC Level 1 or Level 2 Engagement Model Jun Cyber operates under flexible engagement models including: Project-based readiness engagements Ongoing managed compliance operations White-label and partner-delivered services Geographic Coverage Tampa Bay / Florida (local presence) Nationwide (remote delivery with on-site support as required)

description: Anthony Timbers LLC is a premier Consulting Firm and Managed Security Service Provider (MSSP) specializing in providing CMMC-compliant and certified services to contractors within the Defense Industrial Base (DIB). Our comprehensive services ensure that businesses meet the highest standards for protecting controlled unclassified information (CUI) and federal contract information (FCI). We deliver MSSP services specifically tailored to clients requiring CMMC compliance, leveraging top-of-industry tools to ensure robust cybersecurity and regulatory adherence. Operating using only FedRAMP-authorized tools and environments for infrastructure, we provide secure monitoring, incident response, ongoing vulnerability scanning and patching, Data Loss Prevention (DLP) implementation, and full-scale compliance support designed to protect and streamline operations for defense contractors and other organizations handling CUI. Whether it's preparing for CMMC assessments, performing detailed gap analyses, or ensuring compliance with other critical frameworks, Anthony Timbers LLC provides end-to-end solutions to secure your assets and support your growth in the defense sector.

She holds more than 15 industry-recognized certifications—including Lead CCA, CCA, CISSP, CISA, CISM, CRISC, PMP, CDPSE , CCP, and Provisional Instructor (PI) . Her credentials reflect deep expertise across cybersecurity, risk management, audit, compliance, governance, and agile project management. As the visionary founder and CEO of Captiva Solutions , Eberechi has led the organization to become a trusted cybersecurity training and consulting provider, earning designations as an Approved Training Provider (ATP), Approved Publishing Partner (APP), Registered Practitioner Organization (RPO), and Candidate C3PAO within the CMMC ecosystem. Captiva Solutions delivers a broad spectrum of services including regulatory compliance, program management, readiness assessments, and technical training aligned with frameworks such as CMMC, NIST RMF, NIST CSF, FedRAMP, DFARS , and HIPAA . Captiva also specializes in developing comprehensive security documentation including System Security Plans (SSPs), Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms), policies and procedures , and SPRS scoring . Eberechi’s dynamic and interactive teaching style empowers learners through expert facilitation, real-world context, and hands-on exercises that transform complex theories into actionable skills. She is the creator of the Real-Skills-for-Real-Jobs® (RS4RJ®) methodology, a practical instructional approach that equips students with the capabilities needed to succeed in today's threat landscape. She has personally trained and mentored hundreds of professionals nationwide and developed Captiva’s signature CMMC Champions™, Leaders™, and Brass Tacks™ programs to support executives, corporate teams, and individuals in building cyber maturity. Her reach extends across multiple industries, including government contracting, banking, transportation, healthcare, utilities, and more. A recognized strategist and thought leader, Eberechi has served in leadership roles with professional associations such as ISACA and the Project Management Institute (PMI) , and has taught as an adjunct professor at the University of Maryland Global Campus . Her commitment to continuous learning and workforce development continues to shape the future of cybersecurity professionals across the country. description: Mike Parsons holds the CISSP, PCIP, IAM, IEM and is HIPAA certified. He is a 6- year veteran of USMC and resides in eastern North Carolina. Parsons founded BlueTeamAssess LLC in 2015 and is its Senior Cybersecurity Architect and Mentor. His passion is working with small businesses and his vision is to provide affordable and actionable cybersecurity solutions that serve both small and large businesses. He believes information security has a tactical and strategic value proposition for any organization and must not be viewed as a discretionary expense. His areas of expertise are in information technology, cybersecurity, vulnerability and risk management, networking and small business counseling and planning. Parsons has been actively involved in Information Security since the early 1990s. His professional career has included the roles of customer, subject matter expert for networking and cybersecurity, project manager, technical sales, professional services, and entrepreneur. With this background, Parsons has been able to develop a deep understanding of the respective roles of the vendor, the service provider and the customer. He understands the challenges faced in network and systems infrastructure, cybersecurity, and their impact on the organization. Currently, Parsons focuses on four major areas where technology plays a major role and compliance with government and State regulations is of key importance. Cybersecurity best practices and standards in the Defense Industrial Base (DIB) where there are national efforts to protect our Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) through the requirements of SP 800-171 and the soon to be finalized CMMC framework HIPAA requirements found in the General Administrative Requirements, Security Rule and Privacy Rule that impact all health care covered entities and their business associates PCI DSS which establishes cybersecurity and data security requirements for organizations who accept credit cards and debit cards for payment for goods and services GLBA which became law in 1999 to modernize and secure many of the technology practices used by financial institutions and certain insurance services. The GLBA safeguards rule underwent significant changes in 2022 which increased its reach, clarified its requirements and enhanced enforcement. Parsons earned his BA from ECU, his MBA from the University of Maryland and a graduate certificate in Information Security and Privacy from UNC at Charlotte. He is a Senior member of the ISSA and a Platinum member of ISACA. Parsons installed the first firewall at Wachovia and served as the primary security engineer and architect for Wachovia's first Internet banking and brokerage products. He has spoken before several local organizations on the subject of risk and vulnerability management and topics of current concern in information security. He has led many risk assessment efforts and has developed security standards for technical devices and operating environments in major organizations including government, retail and finance. His passion is helping SMBs address the threats encountered from the Internet and understand the risks they face in their daily operation. Parsons has spoken throughout North Carolina on topics that address the needs of small businesses to develop an active cybersecurity program to protect their business, their employees and their customers. As part of his efforts to give back to the business community, Parsons is involved in the following community and volunteer activities: Past President of Triad Chapter of ISSA. Board of Directors, North Carolina Center for CyberSecurity Advisory Council, UNCW Center for Cyber Defense Education Mentor and Course Facilitator for Virtual Cybersecurity Apprenticeships, IQ4 Small Business Mentor and Roundtable Facilitator, SCORE Board of Directors, Swansboro Area Chamber of Commerce Significant achievements- Deployed first firewall in Wachovia Bank in Winston-Salem in 1996 and designed the security architecture to protect its online banking and brokerage solutions Developed baseline security standards for Lowe's Home Improvement Conducted risk assessment of Yadkin Valley Bank and used findings to justify its first full-time security team participated as a company representative in technical trade associations such as Financial Services Technology Consortium, Financial Services Information Sharing and Analysis Center, North Carolina Bankers Association and EastPay, an ACH trade association. As both adjunct and full-time instructor at 4 year and community colleges, taught and mentored many students, several of whom now have leadership roles in technology North Carolina. Developed and implemented security awareness training for both internal employees and business customers Developed and implemented policies, standards and procedures for assessing third party service providers and proposed enterprise applications. Performed numerous vulnerability and risk assessments using such regulatory and industry frameworks such as PCI-DSS, HIPAA, Sarbanes Oxley, Graham Leach Bliley and Federal Financial Institutions Examination Council - FFIEC. Have made many presentations to various audiences that range from the technical lay person and end user to the highly technical engineer and developer.

name: Wheeler, Jace
description: As a Lead CMMC Assessor with over 20 years of military experience and an active security clearance, I am dedicated to securing our nation's defense industrial base and critical infrastructure. My expertise in CMMC, NIST RMF, and Zero Trust architectures, combined with hands-on experience supporting the Department of Defense, equips me to navigate the complexities of cybersecurity and compliance effectively. Having previously owned a small business, I understand the challenges that small and growing companies face, including immediate technical hurdles and the financial burden of maintaining compliance in today’s environment. For many organizations, compliance is not just about meeting standards—it's a matter of survival. Staying ahead of regulations like CMMC and NIST SP 800-171 is crucial, as failure can lead to lost contracts, penalties, or even business closure. I aim to help these businesses align strategic security initiatives with cost-effective solutions that mitigate risk without hindering growth. I have a proven track record of leading complex initiatives that enhance security for the DoD and other federal clients. I have supported key programs like DISA’s Comply to Connect and DoD Zero Trust efforts, developing procedures, training engineers, and providing Tier 3 support for millions of endpoints across the DoDIN and USCYBERCOM. With a Master’s degree in Cybersecurity and certifications in CMMC, CISSP, and more, I am committed to driving results and continuous learning with a relentless focus on compliance, risk mitigation, and operational effectiveness. Influenced by my military background and personal mantra of "Maximum Effort," I bring that same dedication to every project and interaction, ensuring my clients are prepared to tackle today’s complex cyber threats. Cybersec Investments is an Authorized Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) 3 rd Party Assessment Organization (C3PAO) and Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) located in Melbourne, Florida. We are the only Authorized C3PAO on the entire eastern Florida coast. We have nearly 15 years of Department of Defense (DoD) cybersecurity experience. We specialize in assisting organizations in the defense industrial base (DIB) meet CMMC, National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publication (SP) 800-171 and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) compliance.
